level_2_meta_concepts.name: Abductive Reasoning
level_2_meta_concepts.description: The process of making an educated guess or inference based on incomplete information.

level_2_meta_concepts.name: Pattern Recognition
level_2_meta_concepts.description: The ability to identify and describe patterns in data or situations.

level_2_meta_concepts.name: Knowledge Graphs
level_2_meta_concepts.description: A representation of knowledge as a graph of entities and their relationships.

level_2_meta_concepts.name: Problem-Solving Strategies
level_2_meta_concepts.description: Approaches to solving complex problems, including heuristics and decision-making frameworks.

level_2_meta_concepts.name: Statistical Reasoning
level_2_meta_concepts.description: The use of statistical methods to make inferences and decisions.

level_2_meta_concepts.name: Iterative Development
level_2_meta_concepts.description: A process of refining and improving models or solutions through repeated iterations.

level_2_meta_concepts.name: Critical Thinking
level_2_meta_concepts.description: The process of analyzing and evaluating information to form a judgment or decision.

level_2_meta_concepts.name: Computationalism
level_2_meta_concepts.description: The view that the mind can be reduced to computational processes.

level_3_orientations.name: Analytical Problem-Solving
level_3_orientations.description: A focus on breaking down complex problems into manageable parts and using data-driven approaches to inform decision-making.

level_3_orientations.name: Iterative Improvement
level_3_orientations.description: A mindset that values refinement and iteration, recognizing that solutions are often imperfect and can be improved through repeated testing and evaluation.

level_3_orientations.name: Data-Driven Decision Making
level_3_orientations.description: A reliance on empirical evidence and data to inform decisions, rather than relying solely on intuition or anecdotal experience.

level_3_orientations.name: Computationalist Approach
level_3_orientations.description: A view of the mind as a computational system, with an emphasis on breaking down complex problems into manageable parts and using algorithms to solve them.
